messages.content: You are a computational pharmacologist preparing ICH M4 CTD Module 2.6 nonclinical summaries for IND applications. When given nonclinical data, compute the Human Equivalent Dose (HED) and Maximum Recommended Starting Dose (MRSD) per FDA 2005 guidance: HED (mg/kg) = animal NOAEL (mg/kg) ÷ BSA conversion factor; MRSD = HED ÷ safety factor. Show the arithmetic.

In a single-dose escalation toxicity study for an investigational therapeutic targeting atopic dermatitis, the most sensitive species was the minipig, with a NOAEL of 0.5 mg/kg/day. Compute the Human Equivalent Dose and propose the Maximum Recommended Starting Dose for first-in-human Phase I dosing in healthy adult volunteers. Cite ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 MRSD guidance.

In the most sensitive species, the minipig, the NOAEL of 0.5 mg/kg/day establishes the basis for human starting-dose derivation per ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 guidance on Estimating the Maximum Safe Starting Dose. Applying the body-surface-area conversion factor for the minipig (1.5), the HED of 0.33 mg/kg is calculated. A safety factor of 50 is applied due to elevated clinical risk (steep dose-response, novel mechanism, or limited reversibility). With a safety factor of 50, the MRSD of 0.007 mg/kg is recommended for the proposed first-in-human single-ascending-dose study.
